skill.description: Create clinical reports, diagnostic reports, trial documents, and patient notes with templates, regulatory guidance, and local validation scripts for privacy and completeness checks.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by clinical terminology, Markdown backticks, and expected local report-output scripts. No evidence found of command injection, credential access, network calls, or hidden data exfiltration in the reviewed code. Two semantic risks remain: an included self-audit that claims safety and a mandatory external AI figure workflow that could expose clinical data.

remediation.issue: Untrusted self-audit content is included in the package.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_output.json or replace it with neutral test artifacts that do not claim audit approval or safety status.

remediation.issue: External AI figure generation is mandatory for clinical reports.
remediation.suggestion: Make figure generation optional and require de-identified prompts before using scientific-schematics or any external image workflow.

remediation.issue: Local scripts write to user-supplied output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add overwrite confirmation, path normalization, and clear output-directory guidance for all scripts that create files.

content.value_statement: Clinical teams need consistent reports that protect patient privacy and meet publication or regulatory standards. This skill provides templates, checklists, and local validators for case reports, trial reports, diagnostic reports, and patient notes.
actual_capabilities: Drafts CARE-aligned case report sections and patient timelines.
Provides templates for SOAP notes, H&P documents, consult notes, and discharge summaries.
Supports radiology, pathology, and laboratory report structure.
Guides SAE reports and clinical study reports using ICH-E3 and trial reporting conventions.
Includes local scripts for de-identification checks, terminology review, report generation, and adverse event tables.
Provides quality checklists for privacy, completeness, terminology, and regulatory review.
limitations: It does not replace clinician review or medical judgment.
It does not connect to EHR systems or patient databases.
Users must provide de-identified inputs before using external AI tools.
Validation scripts use pattern matching and may miss contextual issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare Case Reports
use_cases.description: Draft CARE-aligned case reports with de-identified patient details, timelines, consent language, and journal-ready sections.

use_cases.title: Document Trial Safety
use_cases.description: Prepare SAE narratives, adverse event summaries, and clinical study report outlines using trial reporting standards.

use_cases.title: Review Report Quality
use_cases.description: Check patient notes and diagnostic reports for completeness, privacy risks, terminology issues, and compliance gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Case Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner template for a de-identified case report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a CARE case report for [condition] using de-identified details. Include title, abstract, timeline, interventions, outcomes, and consent note.

prompt_templates.title: Create a SOAP Note
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate template for patient encounter documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SOAP note for this de-identified encounter: [details]. Organize subjective history, objective findings, assessment, and plan.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Trial Safety Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced template for clinical trial safety reporting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an SAE narrative and safety table summary from this de-identified trial data: [details]. Include causality, expectedness, outcome, and follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Clinical Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for privacy and compliance issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this de-identified clinical report for HIPAA identifiers, unsafe abbreviations, missing regulatory elements, and inconsistent terminology. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: A clinician needs a case report outline for a rare medication reaction.
output: A concise title that includes case report language.
A structured abstract with presentation, diagnosis, intervention, and outcome.
A de-identified patient timeline with key clinical events.
A discussion section comparing the case with published literature.
A consent and privacy checklist before submission.

output_examples.input: A research coordinator needs an SAE narrative from trial notes.
output: A subject-level event narrative with onset, seriousness criteria, treatment, and outcome.
A causality and expectedness assessment section.
A follow-up checklist for sponsor, IRB, and regulatory reporting.
A table-ready summary for adverse event categories.

output_examples.input: A quality lead wants to review a discharge summary before release.
output: A completeness review across diagnoses, procedures, medications, follow-up, and patient instructions.
A privacy check for identifiers and sensitive dates.
A terminology review for prohibited abbreviations and unclear medication wording.
A short list of corrections for clinician approval.

best_practices: Use only de-identified clinical details when drafting or validating reports.
Have a licensed clinician verify every clinical statement before release.
Run privacy, terminology, and completeness checks before sharing reports.
anti_patterns: Pasting identifiable patient data into an external model or image tool.
Treating generated documentation as medical advice or final clinical judgment.
Submitting reports without consent, privacy review, and institutional approval.

faq.question: What report types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports case reports, diagnostic reports, trial reports, SAE reports, SOAP notes, H&P documents, consult notes, and discharge summaries.

faq.question: Does it replace clinician review?
faq.answer: No. A qualified clinician must verify all clinical facts, diagnoses, treatments, and recommendations.

faq.question: Can I use patient identifiers?
faq.answer: Do not use identifiable patient information with external AI tools. De-identify inputs before drafting, reviewing, or generating figures.

faq.question: Which standards are covered?
faq.answer: The materials reference CARE, ICH-E3, ICH-GCP, HIPAA, FDA expectations, ACR guidance, CAP practices, and common documentation standards.

faq.question: What do the local scripts do?
faq.answer: They check de-identification, validate terminology, generate templates, extract simple data, format adverse events, and review report structure.

faq.question: What should I verify before publication?
faq.answer: Confirm consent, de-identification, clinical accuracy, institutional requirements, journal instructions, and regulatory reporting obligations.
